mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (current level) is causally linked to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced discount rates for equity valuation and lower cost of capital for corporate investment.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window for 20-day returns, or 20-day forward returns in low-rate periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% over the past month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises above 5.0% in 1 month, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate and declines in industrial production indicate an emerging economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (UNRATE rising and INDPRO falling) fails to predict negative returns in > 40% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 0.5% for 3 consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during monetary tightening cycles, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (current level) is causally linked to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days through increased consumer confidence and spending on durable goods.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window for 5-day returns, or 5-day forward returns in high-housing-starts periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) below 450,000 million dollars in the last month signals weak consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS falls below 450,000, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate profit pressures.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (current level) is causally linked to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days (approximately one quarter) by supporting sustained corporate investment and economic growth.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window for 60-day returns, or 60-day forward returns in low-rate periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
